title: Effects of Ketone Bodies on Network Stability and Resilience in Humans
summary:
Background

Stress is an important risk factor for many mental health conditions, including anxiety disorders, depression, and stress-related disorders following extreme events. At the same time, people respond very differently to stress. Some individuals remain mentally healthy even under high levels of strain. This ability is referred to as stress resilience.
Recent studies show that stress affects not only mental health but also the body’s metabolism, and that these processes are closely interconnected. There is also growing evidence that stable cooperation between different regions of the brain may form an important basis for stress resilience. In addition, certain naturally occurring substances produced by the body, for example during fasting or physical activity, may play a role in this process. One of these substances is known as a ketone body.

Research Question

The aim of this study is to investigate whether a single intake of such a ketone body changes the stability of brain activity in healthy adults. Furthermore, the study examines whether individuals with higher stress resilience differ in their brain activity and in their response to this metabolic change compared to less stress-resilient individuals. In addition, the study explores whether the protective function between the blood and the brain is related to individual differences in stress resilience.

Methods

Healthy adults whose stress resilience has been assessed over several years take part in this study. Each participant attends two study visits. On one day, participants receive a drink containing the ketone body; on the other day, they receive a drink containing sugar with the same energy content. The order of the two drinks is randomly assigned.
On both visits, brain activity is measured before and after drinking using a painless and non-invasive imaging method. In addition, small blood samples are taken from the fingertip. Results from the two visits are compared to better understand how metabolic processes, brain function, and stress resilience are connected.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Healthy adults from the LORA cohort
- Clinically unremarkable medical history
- Capacity to give informed consent, able to understand the nature and individual implications of the research study
Exclusion criteria:
- Currently or within the last 6 months following a low-carbohydrate or ketogenic diet
- Diabetes or other metabolic disorders
- Regular use of psychotropic medications or recreational drugs
- Cardiovascular diseases
- Blood clotting disorders
- Skin conditions on the hands
- Body mass index (BMI) <18.5 (underweight) or >29.9 (obesity)
- Participation in high-performance sports
- Potential pregnancy
- MRI contraindications
- Insufficient proficiency in German
- Lifetime diagnosis of a severe psychiatric disorder
- Known history of alcohol, drug, or medication abuse or dependence
- Known history of brain injury or neurological developmental disorders, or presence of a neurological disease
- Other serious health problems or current severe mental or physical stress
- Participation in other clinical drug trials during the present study or within the last three months
